# `pattern-added`

Pattern added

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `pattern-added` (both directions), `pattern-added-in-request`, `pattern-added-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A `pattern` was added to a string schema.

## Why this default

In requests: values that do not match are rejected. In responses: clients receive values in a narrower form, which is safe.

## Example

From test case [`pattern-added`](../../test/cases/pattern-added/): A pattern added to a request string.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
+           pattern: ^[a-z]+$
```

Findings:

- `pattern-added-in-request` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  pattern-added: info
```

## How to fix

In requests, keep the value unconstrained.
